text:
Multiracial students made up 11.5% of Dix Street Elementary enrollment in 2024-25
G. N. Haley
Dix Street Elementary School enrolled 41 multiracial students in the 2024-25 school year, 13.9% more than the previous year, according to the Michigan Department of Education.
Dix Street Elementary School had 357 students in the 2024-25 school year. Multiracial students made up 11.5% of the enrollment, the school's second-largest ethnic group. White students were the largest group, making up 82.1% (293) of the student body.
The school is in Otsego Public Schools District, whose central office is in Otsego.
Among the district's six schools, Dix Street Elementary recorded the highest multiracial enrollment in the 2024-25 school year.
Academic performance in Michigan remains below pre-pandemic levels. The 2024 NAEP results show the share of students reaching the basic benchmark in core subjects is about 10 percentage points lower than in 2019—except for fourth-grade math, which declined by 2 points.
Achievement gaps between ethnic groups persist. On average, Hispanic students scored 15 points lower than white students. Black students scored about 30 points lower than their white peers.
